name: Primary Bone Dysplasia with Decreased Bone Density

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Primary Bone Dysplasia with Decreased Bone Density

criteria.description: Radiologic evidence of generalized decreased bone density (osteopenia) on skeletal survey
Recurrent low-trauma fractures during infancy or early childhood
Exclusion of secondary causes of decreased bone density such as metabolic, nutritional, or endocrine disorders
Positive family history of similar bone fragility or dysplasia
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with bone matrix or remodeling

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of radiologic osteopenia and recurrent low-trauma fractures with exclusion of secondary causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may support diagnosis but is not mandatory.

searchTerms: bones breaking easily with low trauma

motor delay caused by fragile skeleton

limb length differences from bone abnormalities

laboratory: Normal serum calcium, phosphate, and alkaline phosphatase levels
Exclusion of metabolic bone disease markers
imaging: Thin cortical bone with increased radiolucency
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes regulating bone matrix proteins or remodeling enzymes (e.g., COL1A1, COL1A2, or others depending on subtype)
other: Bone biopsy showing decreased bone mass with normal mineralization

distinguishingFeatures: Positive genetic testing for COL1A1 or COL1A2 mutations
History of metabolic, nutritional, or endocrine disorders
Abnormal laboratory findings (e.g., hypocalcemia, vitamin D deficiency)
Improvement with treatment of underlying cause

redFlags: Multiple low-impact fractures in infancy or early childhood
Severe bone deformities causing functional impairment
Neurological symptoms suggestive of spinal cord compression
